title: 第 15 课 · 开发板：供电和 GPIO 输入输出
summary: ESP32 开发板怎么上面包板、3V3 / 5V / GND 怎么用、把引脚设成输出点灯、设成上拉输入读按键，以及每个引脚能给多少电流。
concepts: pin current limit 引脚电流
description: 先看「拆开看」里的 **开发板 GPIO**（左侧会自动打开）：推挽输出级、输入、上下拉、3.3 V 稳压。
**这一课学什么**：第 5 期全部是单片机外围电路。这一课先学开发板本身：怎么供电、电源脚怎么用、GPIO 设成输出和输入是什么样子。
**1. 没有程序：“模式”就是程序**
这里的开发板不跑代码，每个 GPIO 在“属性”里选一个**模式**：
| 模式 | 引脚做什么 |
| 输出高 / 输出低 | 输出 3.3 V / 0 V |
| 输入 | 只读电平，几乎不取电流；什么都不接时是**浮空**的，读到的电平不确定 |
| 输入 + 内部上拉 / 下拉 | 内部约 45 kΩ 接到 3.3 V / GND，没接东西时读高 / 低 |
| PWM、ADC | 第 16 课 |
**2. 供电和电源脚**
| 脚 | 电压 | 从哪来 / 用来做什么 |
| 5V | 约 5 V − 0.3 V | 插着 USB 时（默认），USB 的 5 V 经过一只肖特基二极管（压降约 0.3 V）到这里 |
| 3V3 | 3.3 V | 板载稳压器从 5 V 变出来；芯片和 GPIO 都是 3.3 V 的 |
| GND | 0 V | 板上几个 GND 脚在内部是连通的 |
3V3、5V、GND 都可以给面包板供电。
**3. 在面包板上**
ESP32-DevKitC 的两排针插在 b 行和 i 行，中间的孔被板子盖住了——每个引脚只剩 a 行（上排）或 j 行（下排）一个空孔，导线和元件从这里接出去。
- 引脚“输出高”= 一个 3.3 V 电源串联约 25 Ω 的输出电阻：电流越大，引脚电压越低（U_pin = 3.3 V − I × 25 Ω）。
- 每个引脚建议 ≤ 20 mA，超过 40 mA 会损坏——LED 一定要串电阻。
**5. 输入和上拉**
按键一端接 GND、另一端接引脚，再打开**内部上拉**：松开时读高，按下时读低。
**仿真和真实开发板**：这里的输出电阻、上拉电阻和电流上限是固定值；真实 ESP32 的驱动能力可以在程序里设，上拉电阻在 30–80 kΩ 之间，整颗芯片所有引脚加起来还有总电流上限。真实板子上很多引脚有特殊用途（启动配置、串口、Flash），用之前查一下开发板的引脚图。
compare:
**对比**：
- 3V3 脚 ≈ 3.3 V；5V 脚 ≈ 5 V − 0.3 V ≈ **4.7 V**；
- LED 电流 = (3.3 − 1.8) V / (330 + 25 + 12) Ω ≈ **4.1 mA**（25 Ω 是引脚输出电阻，12 Ω 是 LED 内阻）；
- 引脚电压 = 3.3 V − 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ **3.20 V**；由此算出输出电阻 ≈ **25 Ω**；
- 上拉输入：松开读高，按下读低（按下时引脚被按键接到 GND，上拉电阻里流过 3.3 V / 45 kΩ ≈ 73 µA）。

en.title: Lesson 15 · Dev board: power and GPIO in / out
en.summary: Seating an ESP32 dev board, using its 3V3 / 5V / GND, setting a pin as an output to light an LED and as a pulled-up input to read a button, and how much current a pin can give.
description: Look at the **Dev board GPIO** teardown first (it opens on the left): push-pull output stage, inputs, pull-ups, the 3.3 V regulator.

**What you learn**: phase 5 is all microcontroller peripheral circuits. This lesson covers the board itself: how it is powered, how to use its supply pins, and what a GPIO looks like as an output and as an input.
**1. No program: the "mode" is the program**
This board runs no code; each GPIO gets a **mode** in Properties:
| Mode | What the pin does |
| output high / output low | drives 3.3 V / 0 V |
| input | reads a level and draws almost no current; with nothing connected it **floats** and reads an undefined level |
| input + internal pull-up / pull-down | about 45 kΩ inside to 3.3 V / GND, so it reads high / low when nothing is connected |
| PWM, ADC | lesson 16 |
**2. Power and supply pins**
| Pin | Voltage | Where it comes from / what it's for |
| 5V | about 5 V − 0.3 V | with USB plugged in (the default) USB's 5 V reaches it through a Schottky diode (about 0.3 V drop) |
| 3V3 | 3.3 V | made from 5 V by the on-board regulator; the chip and its GPIOs are 3.3 V parts |
| GND | 0 V | the board's GND pins are all joined inside |
3V3, 5V and GND can all power the breadboard.
**3. On the breadboard**
The ESP32-DevKitC's two pin rows go into rows b and i, and the board covers the holes in between — each pin keeps one free hole, in row a (top row) or row j (bottom row), for wires and parts.
**4. Outputs**
- An "output high" pin = a 3.3 V source in series with about 25 Ω: the more current, the lower the pin voltage (U_pin = 3.3 V − I × 25 Ω).
- Keep each pin ≤ 20 mA; above 40 mA it is damaged — an LED always needs a series resistor.
**5. Inputs and pull-ups**
Wire a button from GND to the pin and turn on the **internal pull-up**: released it reads high, pressed it reads low.

**Simulated vs real board**: the output resistance, pull-up and current limits here are fixed values; a real ESP32's drive strength is set in software, its pull-ups are 30–80 kΩ, and the whole chip has a total current limit. Many pins on a real board have special jobs (boot strapping, serial port, Flash) — check the board's pinout before using one.
steps: Pick "ESP32 DevKitC" and click b1 (the GND pin at the top left). The pin rows go into b1–b19 and i1–i19; USB is plugged in by default, so the board is powered. Hover a pin to see its name.
Power the bottom rails from the board: red jumper j1 → bp1 (the 3V3 pin), blue jumper j14 → bn14 (a GND pin). The bottom red rail is now 3.3 V.
The top GND rail too: blue jumper a7 → tn7 (column 7 of the upper row is another GND pin).
Multimeter: red probe on bp5 (the 3V3 rail), then on j19 (the 5V pin). The 5V pin is a little under 5 V — there is a diode between it and USB.
LED circuit: a 330Ω resistor from a15 (GPIO2) to a22.
Red LED, long lead c22, short lead c25; blue jumper a25 → tn25 (GND). The LED is still off: GPIO2 is an input by default.
Click the board and, in the pin list in Properties, set **GPIO2** to "OUT HIGH". The LED lights; the row shows the pin voltage and the current flowing out.
Button: pick "Push button" and click e27 (it straddles the trench: one side on column 27, the other on column 29).
Jumper a13 → a27 (GPIO4 to one side of the button), blue jumper j29 → bn29 (the other side to GND).

GPIO4 is a plain input now: with the button released nothing drives it, and it reads "floating" (see Diagnostics). Set **GPIO4** to "IN pull-up": it reads "high". Click the button with "Select / use" to press it: "low".
Press "Check my circuit" and answer with the multimeter and the pin list.
hints: Each pin has one free hole, in row a (upper row) or row j (lower row); hover a pin to see its name.
Output high = 3.3 V behind 25 Ω: LED current = (3.3 − LED drop) / (R + 25 Ω + the LED's resistance).
Pulled-up input: pulled to 3.3 V when released, tied to GND by the button when pressed.
tests: Output high: LED on; button released reads high

measurements.explain: The USB 5 V passes a Schottky diode first and loses about 0.3 V.

measurements.ask: The LED current (click the GPIO2 row to see the pin current, or put an ammeter in series)
measurements.explain: (3.3 − 1.8) V / (330 + 25 + 12) Ω ≈ 4.1 mA, well under the recommended 20 mA.
The output resistance drops 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ 0.1 V.

measurements.ask: From your readings, the pin's output resistance: (3.3 V − pin voltage) / current
measurements.explain: About 25 Ω. At 20 mA the pin would be down to about 2.8 V — heavy loads need a transistor or MOSFET driver (phase 5 labs).

measurements.ask: GPIO4 set to input with pull-up: what does it read with the button pressed?
choices: low: the button ties the pin to GND; the pull-up can only supply a tiny current
measurements.explain: Released, the pull-up holds the pin at 3.3 V (high); pressed, the pin is tied to GND (low). This is called active-low.

tests.name: 输出高：LED 亮；松开按键读高

measurements.ask: 万用表：5V 脚（j19）对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: USB 的 5 V 先经过肖特基二极管，掉了约 0.3 V。

measurements.ask: LED 的电流（单击 GPIO2 那一行看引脚电流，或者串一个电流表）
万用表：GPIO2（a15）对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 输出电阻上掉了 25 Ω × 4.1 mA ≈ 0.1 V。

measurements.ask: 用你的读数算引脚的输出电阻：(3.3 V − 引脚电压) / 电流
measurements.explain: 约 25 Ω。电流 20 mA 时引脚只剩约 2.8 V——大电流负载要用三极管或 MOSFET 驱动（第 5 期实验）。

measurements.ask: GPIO4 设成“输入 上拉”，按下按键时读到什么？
choices: 低：按键把引脚接到 GND，上拉电阻只能提供很小的电流
measurements.explain: 松开时上拉把引脚拉到 3.3 V（高）；按下时引脚直接接 GND（低）。这叫“低电平有效”。

steps.text: 选“ESP32 开发板 DevKitC”，单击 b1（左上角的 GND 脚）。两排针插在 b1–b19 和 i1–i19；USB 默认插着，板子已经通电。把鼠标停在针脚上可以看名字。
把下方电源轨接上板子的电源：红色跳线 j1 → bp1（3V3 脚），蓝色跳线 j14 → bn14（GND 脚）。下方红轨现在是 3.3 V。
上方 GND 轨也接上：蓝色跳线 a7 → tn7（上排第 7 列也是 GND 脚）。
万用表：红表笔点 bp5（3V3 轨），再点 j19（5V 脚）。5V 脚比 5 V 低一点——USB 和它之间有一只二极管。
LED 电路：电阻 330Ω 从 a15（GPIO2）到 a22。
红色 LED 长脚 c22、短脚 c25；蓝色跳线 a25 → tn25（GND）。LED 还不亮：GPIO2 默认是输入。
单击开发板，在“属性”的引脚列表里把 **GPIO2** 设成“输出 高”。LED 亮了；这一行显示引脚电压和流出的电流。
按键：选“按键开关”，单击 e27（横跨凹槽：一边在第 27 列，另一边在第 29 列）。
跳线 a13 → a27（GPIO4 接按键一边），蓝色跳线 j29 → bn29（按键另一边接 GND）。
GPIO4 现在是普通输入：松开按键时它什么都没接，读“浮空”（“诊断”里有提示）。把 **GPIO4** 设成“输入 上拉”：读“高”。用“选择 / 操作”单击按键按下它：读“低”。
点“检查我的电路”，用万用表和引脚列表完成测量题。

hints: 每个引脚只有 a 行（上排）或 j 行（下排）一个空孔能接线；鼠标停在针脚上看名字。
输出高 = 3.3 V 串 25 Ω：LED 电流 = (3.3 − LED 压降) / (R + 25 Ω + LED 内阻)。
上拉输入：没按时被拉到 3.3 V，按下时被按键接到 GND。
